It's crunch time for retailers — and the challenges this holiday season loom large.

Retailers are up against cost-conscious, cash-strapped consumers demanding greater value, deeper discounts and more conveniences. They're also dealing with rising logistics and fuel costs, shifting tariffs, El Niño disrupting the weather and sudden concerns that the anticipated surge in online retail orders and AI could cause outages, following the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft, and other outages this month.

How Crucial Is Black Friday Weekend to Retailers?

Yet the positive outlook for decent holiday sales gains remains intact — at least for now — with consumers showing resilience so far and a greater inclination to visit stores, a trend particularly true for Gen Z. They're helping retailers keep it together. Positive third-quarter results from Walmart, Target, Abercrombie & Fitch, Gap brand, and even Kohl's, as well as lower temperatures this week, suggest there's momentum ahead of Black Friday.

Retailers also have 29 days between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year, one more than last year.

Toys are selling at Kohl's following improvements in the presentation.

Coats and cold-weather merchandise have not been selling well, but consumer demand for rainwear and wet-weather categories will increase this holiday weekend, according to Planalytics, which advises retailers on the weather and its impact on business. "Overall, the weather over the entire Black Friday weekend will favor winter-driven categories such as outerwear, boots, hats and gloves, blankets and seasonal food and beverages as shoppers respond to both promotions and the more wintry feel," said Evan Gold, executive vice president of global partnerships and alliances at Planalytics.

"By midweek colder air will slide across the central and eastern U.S. and the West will turn warmer again. Finally the colder air will settle over the Southeast at the end of the week and warmer conditions will prevail over the rest of the U.S. Rain will fall in the East and West Coast for much of the week, including heavy rain and high winds in the Midwest and Northeast on Thanksgiving Day and into Black Friday, including New York City, Boston and Philadelphia. Most of the U.S. will be warmer than last year and warmer than normal with a sliver of colder anomalies along the Gulf Coast. Showers will continue near all three coastlines, while the interior of the country is dry."

Coatue Management's November 16 regulatory filing puts billionaire Philippe Laffont's positioning back in focus as investors look toward 2027. Its ten largest disclosed stock holdings represented 55.9% of a $54.5 billion reported portfolio at September 30, with chipmakers and equipment suppliers carrying much of the exposure.

In its May 6 public-markets update, Coatue highlighted the expanding token economy and identified AI agents as the industry's next major opportunity. That theme reaches beyond chip designers. Our look at AI holdings shared by two billionaire investors follows the spending into manufacturing equipment and electricity.

Those connections carry different risks. Infrastructure orders can support suppliers while construction bills pressure their customers' cash flow. A larger holding can also reflect price gains rather than fresh purchases. As with other high-conviction technology portfolios, the question for 2027 is whether growing demand will produce the earnings investors already expect.

Recently, we created a video looking at the 10 stocks billionaires Dalio and Laffont love. You can click below to see these stocks in our video on YouTube:

For our broader look at Coatue's largest positions, see our article 10 High-Conviction Stocks Billionaire Philippe Laffont Is Betting On for 2027. Below, we present the five highest-ranked stocks from that list.

Our Methodology

To compile our list, we reviewed Coatue Management's Q3 2026 13F filing and identified its ten largest stock holdings as of September 30, 2026, excluding ETFs and options. We used each holding's weight in the reported portfolio as a proxy for investment conviction and ranked the stocks from lowest to highest based on the value of Coatue's stake. We also included portfolio weights, changes in shares held from the previous quarter, and Q2 2026 hedge fund holder counts from Insider Monkey's database.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points (see more details here).

5. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Coatue Management's Stake: $3.26 billion

Portfolio Weight: 5.98%

Market Capitalization: $263.36 billion

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) sells the equipment that deposits and removes materials as chipmakers build increasingly complicated devices. More layers and more demanding production steps can mean additional work for its tools, making the company a way to follow the manufacturing investment behind AI.
